import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    df = inputs["payments"].copy()

    amount = df["amount"]
    currency = df["currency"]
    country = df["country"]

    # Rule evaluation in strict order; later rules only evaluated if
    # earlier rules did not already trigger a rejection (short-circuit).
    mask_r1 = amount.isna()

    mask_r2 = (~mask_r1) & (amount <= 0)

    # SQL-style NOT IN semantics: if currency is NULL the comparison is
    # unknown (not TRUE), so it does not trigger this rule.
    mask_r3 = (
        (~mask_r1)
        & (~mask_r2)
        & currency.notna()
        & (~currency.isin(["USD", "EUR", "GBP"]))
    )

    mask_r4 = (~mask_r1) & (~mask_r2) & (~mask_r3) & country.isna()

    reject_mask = mask_r1 | mask_r2 | mask_r3 | mask_r4
    clean_mask = ~reject_mask

    reason_code = np.select(
        [mask_r1, mask_r2, mask_r3, mask_r4],
        ["AMT_NULL", "AMT_NONPOS", "CCY_INVALID", "CTRY_NULL"],
        default=None,
    )

    payments_rejects = df.loc[reject_mask, ["payment_id", "amount", "currency", "country"]].copy()
    payments_rejects["reason_code"] = pd.Series(reason_code, index=df.index)[reject_mask]

    payments_clean = df.loc[clean_mask, ["payment_id", "amount", "currency", "country"]].copy()
    payments_clean["amount"] = payments_clean["amount"].round(2)

    return {
        "payments_clean": payments_clean.reset_index(drop=True),
        "payments_rejects": payments_rejects.reset_index(drop=True),
    }
